claims.claimText: University-wide: Level 2 and above confidential data (including non-public research data, finance, HR, student records, medical information) should not be entered into publicly-available generative AI tools. Such data may only be entered into generative AI tools that have been assessed and approved by Harvard's Information Security and Data Privacy office.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: You should not enter data classified as confidential (Level 2 and above, including non-public research data, finance, HR, student records, medical information, etc.) into publicly-available generative AI tools, in accordance with the University's Information Security Policy. Information shared with generative AI tools using default settings is not private and could expose proprietary or sensitive information to unauthorized parties. Level 2 and above confidential data must only be entered into generative AI tools that have been assessed and approved for such use by Harvard's Information Security and Data Privacy office.

claims.claimText: HGSE (Harvard Graduate School of Education) school-level policy: Unless otherwise specified by the instructor, using generative AI to create all or part of an assignment (e.g., paper, memo, presentation, short response) and submitting it as one's own work violates the HGSE Academic Integrity Policy. Permissible uses include seeking clarification on concepts, brainstorming ideas, or generating scenarios that help contextualize learning.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Unless otherwise specified by your instructor, it is a violation of the HGSE Academic Integrity Policy to use generative AI to create all or part of an assignment for a course (e.g., a paper, memo, presentation, or short response) and submit it as your own. Permissible uses of generative AI in HGSE coursework include seeking clarification on concepts, brainstorming ideas, or generating scenarios that help contextualize what you are learning.

claims.claimText: HGSE (Harvard Graduate School of Education) school-level policy: For any permitted use of generative AI tools, students must acknowledge and document that use in their assignment submission by explaining what tool(s) were used, prompts provided, and how the output was integrated into the work. Direct citations must use proper citation format.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: For any permitted use of GenAI tools, you must acknowledge and document that use in your assignment submission by explaining what tool(s) you used, prompts you provided (if applicable), and how you integrated the output into your work. If you cite directly from the tool, use proper citation format to credit the source.

claims.claimText: HGSE (Harvard Graduate School of Education) school-level policy: It is forbidden to make personal recordings of any course meetings, with or without AI tool integrations. Uploading substantial course content is only allowable through the Harvard-approved AI Sandbox.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: It is forbidden to make your own recording of any course meetings, with or without AI tool integrations. If you require or would prefer that course meetings be recorded, discuss this request with your instructor. Uploading any substantial course content — including text, video, readings, discussion-board pages, or audio recordings — is only allowable through the Harvard-approved AI Sandbox.

claims.claimText: FAS (Faculty of Arts and Sciences) Office of Undergraduate Education guidance: Faculty must get documented permission from students before putting original student content into any generative AI tool. No confidential information can be loaded into generative AI systems since there is no expectation of privacy or confidentiality.

snapshot.summary: Check your Harvard course or unit policy before using AI; Harvard-wide data guidance restricts confidential information to approved tools, while HGSE and HMS rules add scope-specific disclosure and research requirements.

dimensions.summary: Harvard-wide guidance and FAS guidance emphasize clear faculty communication of permitted AI use. Scope: university guidance plus FAS course communication, not a universal permission rule.

do: Check the course or assignment policy posted by the instructor.
dont: Do not treat a different Harvard school policy as your course rule.

dimensions.summary: No source-backed exam-specific student rule is included in this candidate; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
HGSE requires acknowledgement and documentation of permitted AI use. Scope: Harvard Graduate School of Education assignments, not all Harvard courses.

do: Follow the cited HGSE acknowledgement format when that policy applies.
dont: Do not extend HGSE disclosure wording to another Harvard unit without checking it.

dimensions.summary: Harvard-wide guidance restricts Level 2 and above confidential information to assessed and approved generative-AI tools; public tools are not the default path for Harvard work.

do: Check Harvard data classification and approved-tool status first.
dont: Do not enter confidential Harvard information into a public AI tool.

dimensions.summary: Harvard lists offered versions such as AI Sandbox, Gemini, Copilot Chat, ChatGPT Edu, and Firefly with stated data protections. Tool availability does not decide course or assessment permission.

do: Use only the Harvard-offered version and context covered by the cited classification.
dont: Do not infer academic-use permission from the approved-tools list.

dimensions.summary: HMS integrity guidance says AI tools cannot be authors and AI use in research should be transparent. Scope: Harvard Medical School guidance.

do: Disclose how AI was used when the HMS guidance applies.
dont: Do not list an AI tool as a paper author.

limitations: This tracker is not legal advice, not academic integrity advice, and not an official university statement unless a linked source is the university's own official page.

Scope follows the cited source role and unit. A faculty, school, department, course, assessment, library, or staff rule is not generalized university-wide.
English is canonical. Source evidence may be multilingual; no translation is provided or independently reviewed in this candidate.
A university-provided, licensed, or listed tool is not by itself permission to use it in a course, assessment, thesis, or research project.
